samples.summary: A transient Actions/Checks API read error now FAILS the promote job, which the out-of-diff `stalled` job turns into a permanent `agent-review-paged` latch (terminal `blocked`) for the PR
samples.evidence: mark-ready.mjs's gate 1 and gate 2 read failures changed from `return false` (exit 1 → benign "leaving as draft", recoverable on the next round) to `process.exit(2)` (scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:188 and :309). The promote job's new `case` maps 2 → `exit 2`, so the job FAILS. The consumer of that failure is not in the diff: `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:2309` runs `stalled` on `needs.promote.result == 'failure'`, and at :2402 it selects the reason 'the ready-gate (promotion) step errored' and at :2416 posts `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` — "The review panel will not run again on this PR … the ready gate will not promote it." That marker is read by scripts/agent/set-state.mjs:251 into `reviewPagedLatch`, which `deriveState` (set-state.mjs:125) maps to `blocked`, a state TRANSITIONS (set-state.mjs:105) documents as terminal and only escapable with `--force`. So a single 502 on `commits/{sha}/check-runs` or on `/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs` now permanently ends the autonomous loop for that PR, where before it merely deferred promotion by one round. If the page is intended for these classes, the `stalled` reason/latch path needs to distinguish 'evidence unreadable, retry' from 'pipeline broken'; the fix most likely belongs on the new exit-code choice in mark-ready.mjs.

samples.summary: Two of the six `workflows: ["CI"]` consumers were left without the new `workflow_run.path` clause
samples.evidence: The change adds `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` to agent-iterate-ci.yml:54, agent-review-panel.yml (gate) and ci-report.yml:56, and the new checks.test.mjs test pins exactly those three. The other two consumers of the same display-name trigger are unguarded: publish-ghpage.yml:41-47 and docker-publish.yml:67-72. Both rely on `event == 'push' && head_branch == 'main' && head_repository == github.repository`, i.e. the forged `name: CI` file would have to be merged to main first — which is the argument ci-report.yml's new comment makes — but the guard is now inconsistent across siblings and nothing pins these two, so a future relaxation of the `branches:`/`event` clauses silently re-opens them. searchedFor: grep `workflow_run:` across .github/workflows, read docker-publish.yml:56-72 and publish-ghpage.yml:35-47.

samples.summary: capture-collect's new job-level `if:` clauses skip the whole collection SILENTLY, contradicting that file's own stated invariant that an unexpected skip must go red
samples.evidence: capture-collect.yml:31-36 states the subsystem's contract: "COLLECTING NOTHING LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE HAVING NOTHING TO COLLECT … this job goes RED on any skip that should not have happened", and the steps below implement that with explicit failures on unexpected skips. The two new clauses (`head_repository.full_name == github.repository` and the two-path allow-list, capture-collect.yml:141-143) refuse by SKIPPING the job, which is a green, silent no-op — the exact failure mode the header says this subsystem has hit three times. Concretely, if the panel's `workflow_run`-triggered run ever reports a `head_repository` other than the base repo (it inherits the triggering CI run's head), or if either producer file is renamed, captures stop arriving with no red run and only the nightly sweep (which has its own 7-day window) as backstop. Nothing outside the new test asserts the allow-list stays in step with `workflows:` display names.

samples.summary: Gate 1b's new hard requirement that the PR target the default branch changes the promotion contract for any stacked/non-main-based agent PR
samples.evidence: mark-ready.mjs:244 now refuses (exit 1, PR stays draft forever unless a human promotes) any PR whose `baseRefName` is not the repository default branch. I could not find a producer in-repo that opens agent PRs against a non-default base (scripts/agent/spec-to-pr.mjs:228 prints `--base main`), so today this is inert — but the refusal is stderr-only and the loop-status note the panel writes for it is the generic "a ready gate was not satisfied", so if any stacked-PR workflow is added or used manually, the PR silently never promotes and the reason is buried in a step log rather than in the sticky comment.

samples.summary: `gatherSignals` now yields a normalised ci conclusion, narrowing the documented `signals.ciConclusion` shape other readers of that contract assume
samples.evidence: set-state.mjs:234 replaces the raw `ci.conclusion` with `ciConclusion(runs)`, which collapses every non-success (`cancelled`, `timed_out`, `action_required`, …) to the literal `"failure"`. The signal's contract is documented at set-state.mjs:117-121 and exercised at scripts/agent/set-state.test.mjs:83-99 with raw-looking values. The only consumer, `deriveState` (set-state.mjs:129), compares against `"success"` only, so behaviour is unchanged today — but the doc comment and the tests still describe the pre-change shape, and any future reader that wants to distinguish `cancelled` from `failure` can no longer do so.

verdict.reason: Every cited location checks out. mark-ready.mjs:188 and :309 do `process.exit(2)` on a failed `gh api` read of `/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs` and `commits/{sha}/check-runs`, and ghJson (mark-ready.mjs:113-119) has no retry, unlike the `retries: 3` used on github-script steps elsewhere (agent-review-panel.yml:2352, agent-rerun.yml:77) — so one transient 5xx reaches these branches. agent-review-panel.yml:1543 maps exit 2 to `exit 2`, failing the promote job; the out-of-diff `stalled` job triggers on `needs.promote.result == 'failure'` (:2330), selects the reason at :2402, and posts `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` at :2416. That marker is read at set-state.mjs:251 into `reviewPagedLatch`, mapped to `blocked` at :125, a state TRANSITIONS documents as terminal at :105; the panel gate itself also latches on the marker (agent-review-panel.yml:233-250, setting managed=false so no further round runs), and clearing it requires a maintainer's `@claude rerun` (agent-rerun.yml:1-7, 74-85, 144-158). So a transient evidence-read error now converts into a human-only terminal halt of the loop — a behaviour change whose consumers live entirely outside the diff, which is this lens's lane. The author's comments (mark-ready.mjs:176-188, 274-286) show the job-failure was intended but say nothing about the terminal latch. The reviewer's characterisation of the prior behaviour ('recoverable next round') may be too generous — the old `return false` plausibly produced a silent draft — but that does not make the new reachable terminal-latch path unreal, and no named refutation ground applies.

searchedFor: grep for CI_DEFINING_PATHS / definesCi consumers repo-wide
finding.summary: Gate 1b's CI_DEFINING_PATHS omits files ci.yml executes from the merge ref — `Dockerfile.playwright` is the whole browser lane, and a branch may edit it and still auto-promote
finding.evidence: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:528` runs `docker build -t wafflebase-playwright -f Dockerfile.playwright .` and `:533` runs that image as the entire `verify-browser (22.x)` lane. Both come from the PR MERGE REF, exactly like `ci.yml` itself. `Dockerfile.playwright` is not matched by any entry in `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:123-135), so `definesCi("Dockerfile.playwright")` is false and `ranBaseCiDefinition` (scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:222) returns true. A branch whose Dockerfile CMD is `true` produces a genuinely green CI run at the genuine path, gate 1 passes, gate 1b passes, and mark-ready posts the hand-off comment that now asserts "the CI definition that run executed came from `main`" (scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:382-388). The same holds for `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` and `packages/design-sandbox/vitest.config.ts`, which choose which tests vitest collects for those lanes. The fix belongs on the new code: add these paths to CI_DEFINING_PATHS (and, since checks.test.mjs asserts the mirror is a superset of `harness.config.json`'s `ci.ciConfig`, the extra entries are already permitted there). Note the doc's admitted residue is "a branch can weaken its own tests"; a Dockerfile that defines the lane's entrypoint is not test content, so this is inside the claim the gate makes, not the residue it disclaims.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: CI_DEFINING_PATHS (scripts/agent/checks.mjs:123-135) contains no entry matching `Dockerfile.playwright` (or `packages/*/vitest.config.ts`), and the anchored matcher at checks.mjs:140-153 (`*` does not cross `/`) cannot match it indirectly. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:528` builds that Dockerfile from the merge ref and :530-537 runs the resulting image with no command override, so Dockerfile.playwright:7's CMD is the entirety of the `verify-browser` lane. harness.config.json:52-62 (`ci.ciConfig`) also omits it, so there is no mirrored coverage, and checks.test.mjs:492-512 only demands a superset, so adding it is permitted. mark-ready.mjs:205-226/236-288 shows gate 1b's sole refusal input is `definesCi()` on the PR file list, with no other path-based guard, and agent-review-panel.yml:1508 invokes mark-ready with no extra refusal. changed-areas.test.mjs:204-209 confirms Dockerfile.playwright is an unmapped path that forces full+heavy, so the branch's image is what the required lane actually runs. Every other repo-wide Dockerfile reference (scripts/run-browser-tests-docker.sh:62, packages/frontend/scripts/hunt-ui-runner.mjs:8) is a version-pin check, not a promotion gate; the .trusted copy of checks.mjs has no CI_DEFINING_PATHS. No counterexample exists: a reachable bypass of the new gate 1b guard, blocking under the blast-radius rubric.
